title: pr-925001-add-benchmark-lab-performance-suites-reporting-pipeline-v149
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Add v149 performance suites, representative workload runners, memory profiling baselines, and reporting DAG. Adds dashboards and alerting for regression detection.
body:
Motivation: Add the v149 performance test suites and reporting pipeline to capture mixed-workload behavior, memory and kernel-selection profiling, and integrate representative workload runners into the reporting DAG. This improves our ability to detect regressions across throughput/latency/cost and correlates kernel-selection profiles with performance.

What this PR does:
- Adds new performance suites (v149) that include mixed short/long-turn, streaming, and embedding-heavy scenarios.
- Introduces memory-profiling baselines and a lightweight runner that captures RSS/allocations at configurable check-points.
- Adds multi-variant representative workload runners (mixed-runner) to better simulate realistic tenant mixes.
- Implements a reporting DAG (benchmark_lab_reporting/v149_dag.py) that schedules runs, ingests results to the reporting bucket, and emits telemetry for dashboards.
- Updates docs and quickstart for running the new suites.

Checklist:
- [x] Add perf suite configs and runners
- [x] Implement reporting DAG and upload steps
- [x] Add telemetry hooks (kernel_profile, mem_profile)
- [x] Docs/README updated
- [x] CI passes for unit/integration tests

Testing and validation:
- Local runs of the v149 suites against the benchmark lab staging cluster (gpu-small) validated latency/throughput expectations.
- Memory profiling data saved and spot-checked for 4 representative models; no regressions observed vs v148 baselines.
- End-to-end reporting run executed in staging; DAG completed and uploaded artifacts to the reporting bucket.

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main, run nightly in staging for 3 days, then enable in production reporting cadence. Telemetry alerts (regression detection) will be enabled in canary mode for one week before escalating.

Notes:
- This PR intentionally keeps runner changes backwards-compatible with existing scheduler contracts. Some future follow-ups (ENG-2151) will add adaptive batching knobs exposed by the runtime.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-2150, ENG-2151, SUP-4321.

review_comments: Ethan Kim: Please add a comment explaining the choice of sampling interval in memory_profiler.py. Also, tests are failing on python 3.9 in CI (timeout), can you increase timeout for the integration test?
Author (Asha Patel): Added inline doc and increased the integration test timeout. The sampling interval default remains 2s to balance overhead vs fidelity; documented rationale in memory_profiler.py.
Priya Rao: The DAG looks good overall, but can we emit an additional telemetry label to identify kernel-selection profile version? Requested a small change to v149_dag.py.

Author (Asha Patel): Added kernel_profile_version label to the telemetry payload and updated the reporting README with an example. Ran the DAG in staging and confirmed the label is present in telemetry.
